payload: {"schema":1,"version":"0.0.53","date":"2026-10-25","lede":"The Flood tab, an Export and Import dialog with sculpt layers as blendshapes, a plane lock with a Plane Trim brush, Crumble for carving strokes, a Twist operator for ribbons and folds, faster async subdivision on the graphics card, polygroups with their own tool card and a source picker that survive remeshing, seamless textures and resized copies from the library, and a tangent-space normal map in the Baker.","highlights":["Flood tab","Export and Import dialog","Gizmo symmetry","Plane lock","Crumble","Twist"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.53","windows":{"url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.53/Klay_Setup_0.0.53.exe","size":397728288,"sha512":"3d64e123862e6cbb98ae97a2afe36cef8b4b1f6692b8f3e742d65beffd69aa40d4b7dfafadc1b240eba27e1f2f523c6ecfa01ba8fde79b46c882b0a2db3afd87"},"mac":{"version":"0.0.53","url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.53/Klay_0.0.53_macOS.dmg","size":512504207,"sha512":"94ae829a6a1849b80b3bb262e25e6200ba227e4f68c9c61c59d617c720e8f5e885a5e6ea087a8fe8a9b3b12471d0d7ff93f9c92adfdbaa20dc12e777928861c6"},"items":[{"g":"n","t":"Flood tab","b":"The Flood tab, in the sidebar's Sculpt group beside Layers and Brush, applies a stack of processes to the whole of the selected polygon mesh, on its current level, with a live preview: Bend, Twist, Taper, Inflate, Smooth, Polish, Clay polish, Noise, Displace texture and more than 20 others. A card at the top shows the mesh it works on, with the same thumbnail as in the outliner, its vertex count and its level, which can be changed from there. Clay polish flattens the surface into planar facets with crisp edges, with a facet angle and sharpness to set how faceted it gets; its Trim style cuts the surface into large flat planes of a chosen size, like the Trim brush, and its Strength goes up to 3. Noise offers 17 of the app's surface patterns, from grunge and veins to marble, wood grain, rust and scales, with their own contrast, warp and stretch controls. The stack is a list of processes read like layers, each with its icon, its main values, a full-width opacity slider and an on/off switch: the top process runs last, a new one is added on top, and a line is reordered by dragging it. A stack opacity in Output fades the whole stack at once. The selected process opens below the list with its settings, its axis, pivot, mask and symmetry, and a falloff curve along the axis. A process's mask can also be one of the Mask tool's presets, such as Cavity, Curvature or Height; it is recomputed on the shape the process receives, so it follows the processes above it. Apply stack keeps the stack and pauses Live preview, and Apply this switches that process off; Clear empties the stack.","w":["Flood"]},{"g":"n","t":"Export and Import dialog","b":"File > Export, the outliner\u2019s Export selected and Export group, and the export shortcut open one dialog with a tile for every format: OBJ, FBX, GLB, glTF, PLY, DAE, ABC, STL, Maya ASCII and Klay scene. A single pill chooses the whole scene or the selection. On a mesh with sculpt layers, FBX and glTF write the layers as blendshapes and Maya ASCII as a blendShape node, either every layer or a picked set. Formats without blendshapes bake the layers as shown, or also write one file per layer.","w":["File \u203a Export\u2026"]},{"g":"n","t":"Gizmo symmetry","b":"With Symmetry on in the Gizmo tool card and symmetry enabled, moving, rotating or scaling a mesh also applies the mirrored transform to its twin: a separate mesh with the same polygon count at the mirrored position, such as the second eye. One undo restores both.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Gizmo \u203a Symmetry"]},{"g":"n","t":"Plane lock","b":"With a polygon brush, hold R over the model to place a plane on the surface under the cursor; the brush switches to Plane Trim, which shaves only what lies above the plane down to it and leaves everything below untouched, and returns to the previous brush when the plane is turned off. Any other polygon brush chosen while the plane is on stops when it reaches the plane. Keep holding R and move the mouse to tilt the plane; hold R and drag with the right button, or turn the mouse wheel, to move it up or down along its normal. Drag the handle at the tip of the plane's stem to slide it, with Shift to snap and Ctrl for fine steps. A quick tap of R turns the last plane on or off without moving it.","w":["Brush \u203a Polygon \u203a R"]},{"g":"n","t":"Crumble","b":"With Crumble on, a polygon brush that carves, such as Scrape or a brush used with Ctrl, lands part of the removed clay back on the model as small sharp crumbs that pile up in front of the stroke, with a few on the groove's rims. Yield sets how much of the carved clay returns, Front bias how much of it gathers where the stroke goes, and Speed boost adds more crumbs to a faster stroke up to the speed set by Full at speed. The crumbs are made from noise or from a texture, and pen pressure can drive their yield, size and density.","w":["Brush \u203a Stamp & Falloff \u203a Crumble"]},{"g":"n","t":"Twist","b":"The Twist weight in Operator Blend now turns a polygon brush's Draw deposit as the stroke goes. The clay is laid as a side profile drawn in the Twist card, which can fold back over itself, and leans around the stroke, which makes ribbons, folds, waves and braided strands. The weight sets its strength, and a negative weight, or holding Ctrl, gives the mirror image of the shape across the stroke, still raised; Rhythm sets how the angle changes along the stroke. Strength, spacing and build-up act on it as they do on Draw, Smooth on the same brush softens the wave and the profile, and a later pass of the same stroke lies over the earlier one. A Twist brush preset is included.","w":["Brush \u203a Operator Blend \u203a Twist"]},{"g":"n","t":"Tangent-space normal map in the Baker","b":"The Baker can bake a tangent-space normal map from a multires mesh that reads correctly in Blender, Maya, Unreal and Substance. Frame selects Low mesh, for a model rendered without subdivision, or Subdivided low, for use together with a displacement map. Flip green switches the map to the DirectX convention.","w":["Baker \u203a Normal (tangent)"]},{"g":"n","t":"Make seamless","b":"Right-click a texture in the library and choose Process > Make seamless to open it in the viewer with a Seamless card. The picture is shown tiled, with the seams drawn and a before and after split, and updates as the settings change. Cut + Heal follows natural edges such as mortar or cracks, Soft blend suits sand, grass and moss, and Fill rebuilds the seam from the rest of the picture.","w":["Library \u203a Process \u203a Make seamless"]},{"g":"n","t":"Resize copies","b":"Process > Resize copies writes smaller copies of the selected pictures at the standard sizes from 16K down to 256, or at half or a quarter of each file. The resolution in a file name, such as 8k, 4K or 4096, is replaced with the new size in the same style, or added when the name has none, and a table lists every file before it is written.","w":["Library \u203a Process \u203a Resize copies"]},{"g":"n","t":"Brush accessibility","b":"An Accessibility card at the bottom of the Brush tab marks what a clay or polygon brush was made for. A brush marked VR is shown greyed out on the monitor, with a Balanced for VR tooltip, and can still be used. A polygon brush marked Poly only is greyed out while a clay layer is selected, and its strokes are not applied to clay.","w":["Brush \u203a Accessibility"]},{"g":"i","t":"One Boolean panel for clay and polygons","b":"Blend is now part of Boolean. Boolean in the outliner, or the Boolean shortcut, on clay objects opens the same Boolean panel as on polygon meshes, with the clay live in the viewport. The fourth operation is Extract, and a Join section sets the profile of the seam: Round, Chamfer, Muscle, Groove, Weld or Inflate, each with its own sliders and curve. Apply, Enter or D applies; Close or Esc cancels. The sidebar no longer changes to a Blend card, and D still merges selected clay at once.","w":["Outliner \u203a Boolean"]},{"g":"i","t":"Right-drag sets brush size and strength","b":"Right-dragging on a brush changes its size (left and right) or its strength (up and down), like holding B or M. A right-click without moving still opens the viewport menu, and the Mask brush keeps right-drag to erase. The Move and Elastique twist is now Ctrl + right-drag, as on the polygon Grab brush.","w":["Viewport \u203a Sculpting"]},{"g":"i","t":"Import size and position","b":"The Import model dialog now offers four sizes: Original, Match scene, Fit this file and, for several files, Fit each, which gives every model the same size at the centre. Position sets where the model lands in any size: Keep, Centre or On ground. Up axis turns the model as it comes in: Z up for files from 3ds Max or CAD, Flip Y\u00b7Z for a ZBrush OBJ that arrives upside-down. Original also takes a file unit, such as cm or m. Export turns the model back and restores the file's size and position.","w":["File \u203a Import"]},{"g":"i","t":"Faster strokes on large polygon meshes","b":"Strokes on large polygon meshes no longer slow down with the brush size, and run at about twice the frame rate in Unlit.","w":["Viewport \u203a Sculpting"]},{"g":"i","t":"Async subdivision, much faster","b":"Subdivide now runs on the graphics card and is much faster, especially at high levels.","w":["Outliner \u203a Subdivide"]},{"g":"i","t":"Retopology keeps polygroups","b":"Keep polygroups, in both Smooth and Sharp, places edge loops on the borders of the mesh's polygroups and gives the new mesh the same polygroups, with their names and colours. It replaces Follow polygroups, which was available in Smooth only and did not carry the polygroups over.","w":["Outliner \u203a Retopology"]},{"g":"i","t":"Mist in a box","b":"Edit in the Mist section shows the universal gizmo on the mist, which now sits in a box with soft edges: move it, rotate it to tilt the layer, and scale it to set its width and depth. Scaling it vertically sets the Thickness. Edge softness controls how gradually it fades at the sides, and the Box toggle returns to the endless floor layer.","w":["Lighting \u203a Volumetric \u203a Mist"]},{"g":"i","t":"Tessellation indicator","b":"While brush tessellation is on, a Tessellation indicator beside the sidebar shows the brush's mode, Densify or Adaptive, with a dot in that mode's colour. Its X turns tessellation off. The toolbar no longer changes colour.","w":["Viewport \u203a Sculpting"]},{"g":"i","t":"Sidebar tabs in groups, view buttons inside the panel","b":"The sidebar's tabs are arranged in five groups at the top of the panel: Sculpt, Surface, Stage, Output and App. The selected group shows its name, and a second row lists its tabs side by side. Each group returns to the tab last used in it, and the mouse wheel over the header steps through the tabs. The Post Processing tab is renamed Filter.","w":["Sidebar"]},{"g":"i","t":"Polygroups","b":"Zones are renamed Polygroups. A mesh card's Polygroups segment lists each set and its polygroups, and New set builds a set from the painted mask, UV shells, UDIM tiles, islands, angle, curvature, normal direction, symmetry, vertex colour and other sources. A selected polygroup can be grown, shrunk, relaxed or smoothed with a live preview, then inverted, merged, split, moved to a new mesh, masked, hidden or deleted, from the list, a right-click or the pastille beside the sidebar. Every entry of a polygroup's right-click menu has an icon. Copy takes the selected polygroups, and Paste, on a polygroup or a set, adds them to that set as new polygroups on the same faces, including onto another mesh with the same topology. The preview stays live while the view is limited to the selection, and the pastille's Mask masks the selected polygroups.","w":["Outliner \u203a Polygroups"]},{"g":"i","t":"Split dialog","b":"The Split dialog shows its main choices at the top: Islands or Polygroups, with the number of each and the mesh's polygroup sets, then Largest, Pick or All. Pick starts with nothing selected. In the viewport, a click selects or drops a part, dragging across parts selects them, and dragging from empty space draws a rectangle or a lasso; Shift adds and Ctrl removes. Invert is a switch that keeps the unselected parts. Select similar adds every part close to the last one clicked, by polygon count, bounding box or both, within a tolerance. Display shows the parts the split removes, ghosts them as see-through, or hides them. Cleanup can delete every part smaller than a percentage of the mesh's bounding box. Result holds Group parts, Compact and Keep original, which leaves a hidden copy of the mesh. Each section folds on its chevron. A new Delete button removes the selected parts and leaves the rest of the mesh in place.","w":["Outliner \u203a Split loose parts"]},{"g":"i","t":"Select tool: loops, hover and gizmo","b":"In Face mode a quad model selects whole quads, and the selection keeps full detail when the camera zooms out.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Select"]},{"g":"i","t":"Faster library with previews and multiple selection","b":"The library keeps small copies of its pictures in a thumbnails folder of the Klay user folder, so it opens faster and loads only the pictures near the visible part of the list. Only that part of the list is built, so a library of thousands of pictures scrolls smoothly. Moving the window and scrolling, including dragging the list with the left or middle button, are smoother: the mouse wheel glides and accelerates on fast turns, and on macOS the trackpad scrolls the list directly under the fingers and keeps coasting after they lift. Holding the pointer over a picture shows a larger preview, and a click or double-click opens it at full resolution over the whole window, with smooth zoom and pan, a minimap while zoomed in, a filmstrip of the category, and a Use button. The viewport stays paused behind it. Info opens an Inspector with the file details, a histogram, clipping, a colour palette, a tiling check and the grade status. A floating Grade card applies the Camera tool's Color Correct to the picture, with the same controls and results as the Post tab, including the histogram, Structure, Clarity, Sharpening and Grain; a graded item shows a badge on its tile that switches the grade on or off, uses the graded version when applied, and Bake\u2026 saves a graded copy next to the original. EXR and HDR pictures appear in the library and open in the viewer with their full range: the Grade card's Exposure, Highlights and Whites recover detail above white, and Bake\u2026 saves them as a 16-bit PNG. Photoshop files (PSD and PSB) appear in colour, 16-bit PSD, TIFF and PNG pictures open and grade at full precision, and 32-bit float PSD and TIFF files open with their full range like an EXR; their baked copies are 16-bit PNGs, and a PSD or a float file is never overwritten. Right-click a picture, in the library or in the viewer, for Color correct: edit, copy, paste, turn on or off, bake or delete a grade, on one picture or a whole selection. Ctrl+click and Shift+click select several items, which can then be dragged to a category, moved or deleted together. Every action in the right-click menu has an icon, and the list has a scrollbar.","w":["Library"]},{"g":"i","t":"Baker levels, layout and 16K maps","b":"Displacement, vector displacement and normal maps always bake from each target's highest subdivision level, and each target row in the Targets card has its own picker for the level it is baked down to. The level shown in the viewport no longer affects the result. Every card has an icon and a darker body, Setup holds Resolution and sampling, Output holds where the maps go, and Resolution now reaches 16384 pixels.","w":["Baker \u203a Targets"]},{"g":"i","t":"Fine slider control","b":"Hold Ctrl while dragging any slider to move it at a tenth of the normal speed. Pressing Ctrl before the drag keeps the current value instead of jumping to the click. With Invert stroke set to Alt, the Alt key does this instead.","w":["All sliders"]},{"g":"i","t":"Gizmo right-drag rotation","b":"Rotating with a right-drag in the Gizmo tool now shows the same angle ruler and readout as the rotation rings. Hold Shift to snap in 5\u00b0 steps, or 15\u00b0 steps further from the gizmo, and hold Ctrl for a finer rotation. The same right-drag rotates the selected control points in the Lattice tool.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Gizmo"]},{"g":"i","t":"Gizmo keeps its shape while dragging","b":"While a gizmo handle is dragged, the other handles stay in place, greyed, instead of disappearing. In Edit pivot the scale handles remain visible but greyed and cannot be grabbed. A tap of Ctrl, with nothing held, turns Edit pivot on or off; with Ctrl and Alt swapped, Alt does this instead.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Gizmo"]},{"g":"i","t":"Camera post-processing on and off","b":"The POST badge on a camera card switches all post-processing on or off for that camera, which looks through the scene's post group unless another one is chosen in its Post-process section. A Post process toggle function can be placed on any button to do the same for the current view. Fast Unlit (F1) always shows the view without post-processing; the Post tab can still be edited there.","w":["Camera \u203a Cameras"]},{"g":"i","t":"Smoothing options in one place","b":"Smooth only while moving, Smooth when moving and Smooth passes have moved from Advanced stroke > Clean-up to the Smooth operator's section of the brush, next to Dynamic by topology.","w":["Brush \u203a Operator Blend \u203a Smooth"]},{"g":"i","t":"Armature tool card: one mode at a time","b":"The Armature tool card shows three modes as icons, Build, Pose and Limits, with a line describing the current mode's gestures, and lists only the settings of the current mode: joint, bone shape and look in Build; physics and the live skin in Pose, along with Bake skin to a new layer; the swing sectors in Limits. While the live skin is shown, the joints and bones are drawn through it.","w":["Tools \u203a Armature"]},{"g":"i","t":"Lattice: new card and cage display","b":"The Lattice card has been redesigned. Point selects control points with a click or a rectangle (Shift adds, Ctrl removes), and Paint moves them with a brush set to Grab, Inflate, Smooth or Relax; it follows pen pressure, Shift relaxes, and B sets its radius. Affect sets whether the cage moves the whole model, keeps the masked part in place, or moves only the faces, edges or vertices selected with the Select tool; the mask can be inverted or removed from the card. Interpolation sets how the deformation spreads between control points, and the cage now shows only its outer edges and corners, with selected points in the accent colour.","w":["Tools \u203a Lattice"]},{"g":"i","t":"Compact mode and subdivision level pop-out","b":"In compact mode, holding the pointer over a mesh's subdivision level opens a larger control with a dot for each level, step arrows and a Subdivide button; scrolling over either one changes the level.","w":["Scene \u203a Compact mode"]},{"g":"i","t":"Sculpt layers above 100 %","b":"Click the percentage of a sculpt layer or a layer folder in the Scene panel and type a value above 100, such as 150 or 300, to boost it. The slider still covers 0 to 100 %, and a boosted value is shown in the accent colour.","w":["Scene \u203a Sculpt layers"]},{"g":"i","t":"Add a brush alpha to the library","b":"Right-click the brush's Alpha stamp card, or the Loaded picture of Alpha grading, and choose Add to library, or Add to library with a category. An alpha loaded from another folder is copied into the library without replacing a different file of the same name, and the brush then uses that copy.","w":["Brush \u203a Stamp & falloff \u203a Alpha stamp"]},{"g":"i","t":"TIFF images everywhere","b":"TIFF files (.tif and .tiff) can now be used wherever an image is loaded: brush alphas, stamps and the mask Image source, stencils, matcaps, material and texture maps, light projector images, Flood displacement maps and the render viewer. They appear in the library and in the file pickers. Compressed files from Photoshop, Substance and other applications are read, at 8 or 16 bits or in 32-bit float.","w":["Library"]},{"g":"i","t":"Texture map colour spaces and normal map formats","b":"Each texture map of a PBR material has a Colour space setting: Auto, sRGB, Linear or Raw, and ACEScg or ACES 2065-1 for the Albedo and Specular maps. Auto keeps the previous behaviour. The Normal map adds an OpenGL or DirectX choice for the green channel, Flip X, the channel layout (RGB, RG or AG) and signed values; a file whose name ends in DX or GL selects the matching convention when it is loaded. EXR and HDR maps keep their full precision, and Browse now also opens EXR, HDR, TIFF and PSD files.","w":["Material \u203a Texture maps"]},{"g":"i","t":"Save as clay stamp","b":"Save as stamp is renamed Save as clay stamp. It now converts the whole mesh to clay before saving, so the stamp keeps the detail of the source mesh, and the view can be moved while it saves. The preview in the library and under the cursor shows the stamp's clay surface, without the inner parts of the source mesh; Preview detail sets its detail.","w":["Scene \u203a Mesh \u203a Save as clay stamp"]},{"g":"i","t":"Measure tool","b":"The Measure card is reorganised into Distance and Angle tiles with one row per choice. Path draws a line straight or over the surface of the model, following its form like a tape measure, and the length is measured along it. Snap places points anywhere on the surface or on the nearest vertex, with a ring that shows where the point will land. Divide marks each line in halves, thirds, quarters or any number of parts. Point shows each point as a dot or as a crosshair that follows the line. Values are shown with three decimal places, and a chain of lines shows its total at the last point.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Measure"]},{"g":"i","t":"Smaller OBJ files","b":"OBJ export no longer writes vertex normals, as in ZBrush: other applications compute their own on import. Files are about half the size, with the same positions, UVs and vertex colours.","w":["File \u203a Export\u2026"]},{"g":"i","t":"Delete hidden after Isolate to mask","b":"Delete hidden now also works after Isolate to mask: it permanently removes the faces outside the mask, as it does for a crop or a polygroup filter. The isolate ends and the other objects are shown again.","w":["Outliner \u203a Delete hidden"]},{"g":"f","t":"Blending two clay objects no longer shows black holes or blocky, stepped patches in the fillet, including when a small object is blended onto a large one. The Melt slider of the Round profile now takes effect."},{"g":"f","t":"Starting a new scene with Don't save after sculpting a polygon mesh no longer crashes on macOS."},{"g":"f","t":"The Flood tab's Mask preset list now has a search field and a scroll bar, and it scrolls smoothly, so every mask preset can be found. It opens on the current choice."},{"g":"f","t":"Dragging objects in the outliner now changes their order. A duplicated mesh can be placed among the other meshes, and an object can be dragged to the bottom of the list; before, these drops left the object where it was."},{"g":"f","t":"Retopology no longer stays at 70% for minutes, crashes, or ends without a result on a mesh with folded or overlapping surfaces, such as a voxelized model whose holes could not all be closed. It repairs the mesh first, Cancel works at every step, and a failure now shows a message."},{"g":"f","t":"Voxelize now warns when the source still has open borders after closing them, since the result is hollow or double-walled there."},{"g":"f","t":"Retopology on an open surface, such as a single-sided disk, now keeps the open border as a clean edge loop instead of closing it with a second layer of faces, in both Smooth and Sharp."},{"g":"f","t":"Renders at an aspect other than the window's, such as 1:1, 4:5 or 9:16, are no longer squeezed; the image now matches the camera's frame."},{"g":"f","t":"Pen input on Automatic now uses Windows Ink for every tablet other than Wacom, such as Huion and SuperDisplay, so their pens respond and mouse clicks on the interface are no longer ignored. Wintab compat in Settings > Tablet still forces Wintab."},{"g":"f","t":"Draw and the other swept polygon brushes no longer break into square chunks when a stroke runs along the side of a form."},{"g":"f","t":"Polygroups by UV shells now follow the UV seams; a mesh without UVs is refused instead of giving the same result as Islands."},{"g":"f","t":"Polygroups by symmetry now split on the symmetry plane instead of the object's origin, and polygroups by curvature work on every mesh."},{"g":"f","t":"Growing or smoothing a polygroup while other polygroups are hidden no longer makes parts of the mesh flicker; the hidden part updates when you release."},{"g":"f","t":"In the Material tab, a row of the material list no longer shows through the material card at the bottom of the panel."},{"g":"f","t":"Ctrl-rotating with the polygon Grab brush now keeps turning past a full turn instead of snapping back at 360\u00b0."},{"g":"f","t":"Grab with Reach set to Topology no longer pulls nearby separate pieces, such as an eye beside the eyelid, and no longer shows a box-shaped falloff around the cursor on dense meshes."},{"g":"f","t":"Holding Shift to smooth no longer switches the Brush tab to the Smooth brush; it keeps showing the brush in use."},{"g":"f","t":"An alpha imported from the brush's Alpha stamp card now appears in the library and its recent list at once."},{"g":"f","t":"The brush setting Strength x is renamed Strength multiply."},{"g":"f","t":"Voxelize no longer leaves triangles where two areas of its quad grid meet; the result is made of quads except for a few isolated triangles."},{"g":"f","t":"Brush tessellation on a mesh with UVs no longer opens holes along the UV seams, including on meshes imported from FBX, glTF and Collada."},{"g":"f","t":"Area lights in PBR and PBR Fast now match their Path Tracing brightness, including the effect of the panel's size and angle."},{"g":"f","t":"A bake no longer stops responding when a target mesh cannot change subdivision level."},{"g":"f","t":"Subdividing to a level that would need more graphics memory than is free now asks first, with the amount needed and available, instead of risking a crash."},{"g":"f","t":"Settings > Brush cursor has a Crease brush dots toggle for the groove dots that Skin and other crease brushes draw on the cursor, and the Centre dot now goes up to 10 px."},{"g":"f","t":"The brush cursor for Select tool painting and for masking clay layers is now the same surface cursor as sculpting, at the size the brush actually paints."},{"g":"f","t":"Select tool painting in Face, Edge and Vertex modes now selects everything inside the brush cursor, not only its centre, and the gizmo hides while B or M is held so the resize cannot catch a handle."},{"g":"f","t":"In the Armature tool's Pose mode, the joint or bone under the cursor is now filled in the Select tool's selection colour, and the highlight is hidden while dragging."},{"g":"f","t":"In the Armature tool's Pose mode, a right-drag rotates the joint under the cursor instead of the last joint clicked."},{"g":"f","t":"An armature with a skin no longer shows an empty-layer bubble that appears and disappears."},{"g":"f","t":"An armature's skin is now listed nested under the armature in the outliner."},{"g":"f","t":"Saved clay stamps now appear in the library, and deleting an item from the library removes it."},{"g":"f","t":"Renaming an item in the library no longer breaks the brushes, materials, lights and presets that use it; they follow the new name, including colour-corrected copies. MatCap images can now be imported, renamed, duplicated and deleted in the library, and duplicating a picture keeps its file type."},{"g":"f","t":"A clay stamp applied at a large size no longer leaves holes in the clay."},{"g":"f","t":"Masks are now visible on objects with a MatCap material."},{"g":"f","t":"The Mask tool's Open edges source now masks a band along a mesh's open edges only, on triangle and quad meshes alike; it used to cover the whole mesh or nothing. Borders between polygroups are a separate Polygroup borders source."},{"g":"f","t":"The sky now shows behind MatCap materials in PBR Fast and PBR, as it does in Path Tracing."},{"g":"f","t":"With symmetry on, an armature joint placed within one joint radius of the symmetry plane becomes a single joint centred on the plane, and moving a centred joint in Pose keeps it on the plane."},{"g":"f","t":"In Path Tracing, moving the view no longer leaves a faded, offset copy of the previous view over the image, including inside the render region."},{"g":"f","t":"Closing the render region returns to the view mode that was active before it switched to Path Tracing."},{"g":"f","t":"Reshaping a mesh quickly, for example by dragging a Flood, Lattice or curve slider, no longer makes patches of the surface flash out for a moment."},{"g":"f","t":"In the Material tab, rows of the material list no longer show through the material card at the bottom of the panel after switching materials."},{"g":"f","t":"The viewport readouts (frame rate, polygon count) now stay above the animation timeline when it is opened or made taller."},{"g":"f","t":"EXR and HDR roughness, metalness, normal, height and bump maps now read their values correctly instead of brightened."}],"history":[{"version":"0.0.52","date":"2026-10-18","lede":"Stroke deposit engine 2.0, face, edge and vertex selection, updated clay and rake brushes with dynamic smoothing, and finer spacing and stroke direction controls.","highlights":["Stroke deposit engine 2.0","Face, edge and vertex selection"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.52","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Stroke deposit engine 2.0","b":"Polygon brushes stroke up to five times faster on models of 20 million polygons and more. Every brush benefits.","w":["Brush \u203a Polygon"]},{"g":"n","t":"Face, edge and vertex selection","b":"The Select tool card picks Object, Face, Edge or Vertex from a row of icons; holding V with the Select tool opens a wheel with the same choices. Drag on the model to paint a selection, or from empty space to draw a rectangle or lasso. Selected edges and vertices are drawn in the selection colour.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Select"]},{"g":"i","t":"Clay and rake brushes updated","b":"The Clay Hard, Clay Buildup, Wet slab and Rake Dry brushes have been updated and now use Dynamic by topology for their Smooth operator, so they keep the same feel on light and very dense meshes.","w":["Brush \u203a Polygon \u203a Clay Hard"]},{"g":"i","t":"Stroke direction controls","b":"Ignore stroke reversal keeps a print's orientation when a stroke goes back over the same line, so a box no longer turns around at each change of direction. Smoothing sets how far the brush travels before the print turns, which keeps it steady along a nearly straight line.","w":["Brush \u203a Stamp & Falloff \u203a Direction"]},{"g":"i","t":"Dynamic smoothing by topology","b":"A new Dynamic by topology option for the Smooth operator of polygon brushes adjusts the smoothing to the mesh density under the brush, so a brush keeps the same feel from a light mesh to tens of millions of polygons. When it is on, the Smooth value is the one used on a 20-million-polygon mesh and the row reads Smooth (dynamic). Low boost and Max boost add smoothing at the light and dense ends of the range.","w":["Brush \u203a Operator Blend \u203a Smooth \u203a Dynamic by topology"]},{"g":"i","t":"Finer spacing","b":"The first half of the Spacing slider now covers 1 to 10 % of the brush size in steps of 0.1 %; the second half goes from 10 to 1000 %.","w":["Brush \u203a Stamp & Falloff \u203a Spacing"]},{"g":"i","t":"Finer deposit step","b":"The Deposit step of polygon brushes now goes down to 0.001 of the brush radius, shown with three decimals, and the low end of its slider has more travel for small values.","w":["Brush \u203a Advanced \u203a Performance \u203a Deposit step xR"]},{"g":"i","t":"Armature tool card (in progress)","b":"The Armature tool is still in progress, and its card and behaviour may change in coming versions. The Armature tool card shows the five modes as icons, Build, Pose and Angle for the skeleton and Select and Bone for pins, with a line describing the current mode's gestures. Joint size, bone shape, pose physics, pin physics, part materials and the live skin are now in the card, along with Bake skin to a new layer. A new Tap drops setting chooses whether a plain tap in Build places a ball or a hinge; Shift places the other one.","w":["Tools \u203a Armature"]},{"g":"i","t":"Lattice: selection and mask","b":"The Lattice card has two new options. Use Face / Edge / Vertex moves only the faces, edges or vertices selected with the Select tool, and Use mask keeps the masked part of the model in place. Make the selection or mask before switching to Lattice.","w":["Tools \u203a Lattice \u203a Use mask"]},{"g":"i","t":"Subdivision level in the compact outliner","b":"In compact mode, each polygon mesh row shows its current and highest subdivision level, for example 2/6. Scroll over it, or click its left or right side, to change level; at the highest level the right side adds a subdivision.","w":["Scene \u203a Compact mode"]},{"g":"f","t":"Typing in the toolbar drawer's search now also finds the tools of the Tools section, such as Select, Move and Gizmo."},{"g":"f","t":"Typing T in the toolbar drawer's search no longer switches to full screen."},{"g":"f","t":"A polygon brush with a Box shape and Spacing set to Continuous now deposits a box instead of a rounded stroke."},{"g":"f","t":"Brushes with a Box stamp keep the round cursor. The square cursor returns with Square ring for box brushes and Show the alpha as the stamp shape both turned on in Settings > Brush cursor."},{"g":"f","t":"On very dense meshes, Elastique and other brushes with Reach set to Topology no longer stop at a hard edge inside their falloff."},{"g":"f","t":"Duplicates of a polygon mesh no longer render with holes in Path Tracing after the original is edited, and they keep their outliner thumbnail."},{"g":"f","t":"Faces moved with the Select tool's gizmo no longer disappear during the drag."},{"g":"f","t":"Hovering a joint or bone with the Armature tool no longer flickers; it is outlined like an object under the Select tool, and Ctrl over a joint in Build shows the Select tool's red deselect outline."},{"g":"f","t":"Armatures can be deleted from the outliner, with the right-click menu or the Delete key.
